brief: Canned mountain water with a metal-heads attitude. Mostly sold in 12-24 packs. Young audience and anyone who likes edgy branding.

profile.business_summary: Canned mountain water branded with an edgy, metal-head attitude, primarily sold in 12-24 packs to a young audience.
stated_claims: Canned mountain water with a metal-heads attitude.
Young audience and anyone who likes edgy branding.

relevant_tags.why: The product is canned mountain water.
Canned water packs are highly convenience-oriented products.
Canned water in edgy packaging often serves as a non-alcoholic, healthy alternative to soda or energy drinks at social events.
Water is a staple grocery item purchased in bulk packs.
12-24 packs of canned water are typically stored in the pantry.

persona_conflicts.evidence: The brand relies heavily on novelty 'metal-heads' edgy branding.
Advertiser features a 'metal-heads attitude' and 'edgy branding'.

note_signals.why: Swiftcart has late-night traffic spikes and impulse-friendly buyers, which aligns well with an edgy, young beverage brand.
Linden Park has a conservative brand sensibility and older affluent demographic, which directly clashes with a metal-head attitude.
Marlowe & Co. caters to older affluent women with lower impulse behavior, which is the opposite of this brand's young, edgy target.
Beverage-specific host with shoppers seeking alternative, premium drinks.

profile.gate_reason: The product type, packaging format, and target audience are clearly defined, allowing for immediate placement planning.
missing_info: Shipping costs and weight-related fulfillment constraints
clarifying_questions: What is the retail price for your 12-packs and 24-packs?
Do you offer a subscription option for recurring water deliveries?
Are there any shipping restrictions or high shipping fees due to the weight of the liquid packs?

config.advertiser_summary: Canned mountain water branded with an edgy, metal-head attitude, primarily sold in 12-24 packs to a young audience.

assumptions: Price not given; assumed $60 for a 'unknown' product.
repeat_consumable: assumed 2.5 orders per customer over ~6 months.
No target CPA/ROAS or margin given; assumed 50% gross margin (typical for beverages). Give a target CPA to replace this.
Target CPA = 70% of max affordable CAC ($60 x 50% margin x 2.5 orders = $75.00).

pricing.rationale: Acquisition goal with no conversion history: pay per click. Max CPC = target CPA $52.50 x click-to-purchase rate (1.6%-5.6% for beverages). Clicks are observable without trusting a pixel, so both sides can verify billing.
pricing.tcpa_unlock: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.

budget.pacing: even daily pacing; pause a host if CPA > 2.0x target after 150 clicks

allocations.rationale: score 0.28 -> relative fit x1.40 on CTR/CVR; max bid $2.35 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.27 -> relative fit x1.37 on CTR/CVR; max bid $2.29 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.25 -> relative fit x1.30 on CTR/CVR; max bid $2.18 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%
score 0.23 -> relative fit x1.24 on CTR/CVR; max bid $2.08 (break-even at target CPA), start at 70%

warnings: No budget given: recommending $3,140, the smallest budget that buys 300 clicks per host.

phases.name: learning
phases.rule: bid = start bid per host (70% of break-even); pacing adjustment only
phases.why: stable bids so measured CTR/CVR aren't confounded by bid changes

phases.name: enhanced_cpc
phases.until: tCPA unlocks after conversion tracking is verified and 50 click-through conversions are recorded; until then Disco can't predict conversion rate for this brand.
phases.rule: bid = start bid x conversion_likelihood x pacing, clamped to [floor, max bid]
phases.why: spend more on shoppers who look likely to buy, never above break-even

phases.name: target_cpa
phases.rule: Disco bids automatically to hit $52.50 CPA
phases.why: only once Disco can predict this brand's conversion rate

adjustments.reason: Bid higher when the shopper looks like a high converter: their persona match for this campaign vs the host's average shopper (from the serve-time persona posterior).
Under-delivering vs the daily plan -> bid up a little; over-delivering -> bid down.

bid_strategy.rationale: Start below break-even and fixed so the first two weeks measure the hosts, not the bidder; then bid per shopper within a hard ceiling (max CPC = target CPA x CVR), so a single click can never cost more than it's expected to earn.
